inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 31 Mar 2026: 170.600m ordinary shares on issue (FY26 AR line 4619) plus ~2.8m dilutive RSUs/options (diluted WA 175.857m less basic WA 164.588m less 8.436m if-converted note shares, AR lines 3255-3258). The 2031 convertible notes are EXCLUDED from the count and carried as debt at face: initial conversion price USD109.65/share (~A$165 at the fixed AUD/USD 0.6649) is more than 2x the current price, and holders have a year-5 (June 2029) put at par. Count held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). The A$1.85bn placement and the NZ$628m of shares issued to Melio holders are already in the 170.6m.
inputs.debt_note: total_debt is at FACE, not carrying value: 2031 convertible notes principal NZ$1,617.9m (AR line 3986; carried at NZ$1,259.0m amortised cost after a NZ$345.6m unamortised debt discount) plus syndicated facilities NZ$693.7m (AR line 2737, drawn to fund Melio). Cash = cash and equivalents 884.4m + short-term deposits 1,049.8m (AR lines 2698-2699). Lease liabilities NZ$172.3m (33.5 current + 138.8 non-current) are EXCLUDED from net debt under lease treatment (B). The conversion-feature derivative liability and the offsetting call-spread asset are both excluded: at the current price both are deep out of the money and they net to roughly zero economically.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Company-defined free cash flow FY26 (AR line 1519): OCF less investing ex acquisitions, excluding ~NZ$36m of one-off Melio transaction costs paid. The Metrics.csv figure (OCF 933.1 less capex 415.2 = 517.9) includes those one-offs. Owner FCF = 554.0 - 240.1 SBC - 107.0 interest income = 206.9 (on the CSV basis it would be 170.8). The forward build is from components, so last_fcf is an anchor, not a driver.
inputs.sbc_source: FY26 Annual Report line 1491 (share-based payments NZ$240.1m impact on adjusted EBITDA; cash-flow add-back) and line 1475 (adjusted EBITDA ex-SBC 997.4m vs adjusted EBITDA 757.4m). No cash taxes paid on net-share settlement are disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 across the history), so the combined figure equals the add-back. FY26 SBC included ~NZ$45m of non-recurring option grants / sign-on from new remuneration packages (H1 FY26 interim, footnote 7) that management said would largely not recur in FY27; underlying SBC/revenue is ~7.1%.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest income is stripped even though net cash is now ~zero, because the forward build is UNLEVERED (from adjusted EBITDA): neither the NZ$107.0m finance income on the deposit pile nor the NZ$43.5m interest paid on the notes/facility belongs in the flows; both are settled through the net-debt bridge. The deposit pile that earns the income is in `cash` (matching-asset rule).
inputs.buyback_note: No repurchases in any year (ShareRepurchases = 0 FY2015-FY2026). The flat count is a modelling convention the company has not paid for in cash; dilution has historically run ~1%/yr from awards, and that cost is charged here as expensed SBC.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows are NZD (NZ IFRS, Xero Limited, Wellington). The ASX quote is AUD. Rate NZDAUD=X 0.8072 (1 NZD = 0.8072 AUD), Yahoo Finance, 2026-11-07. Per-share values are computed in NZD and converted to AUD by multiplying by 0.8072. No parity check available: Xero delisted from the NZX in Feb 2018 and has no other listed equity line (XRO.NZ returns no data). Management's FY28 aspiration uses NZD/AUD 0.91 constant currency, i.e. the NZD has weakened ~11% against AUD since, which flatters reported NZD growth of the AUD revenue base.
inputs.price_note: ASX regular close Friday 6 Nov 2026 (16:10 AEDT); not an after-hours print. 52-week range 55.09-143.63; the stock is ~50% off its high after the 2026 software/AI de-rating. H1 FY27 results are due mid-November 2026 and will move the FY27 anchors; this build predates them.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in NZD, the currency of the flows. NZ 10-year government bond ~4.6% (Nov 2026), equity risk premium 5.0%, beta ~1.2 for a large-cap growth SaaS name with a net-debt balance sheet post-Melio -> cost of equity ~10.6%. Debt ~NZ$2.3bn at face (~13% of EV at the current price) at ~5.5% pre-tax / ~4.0% post-tax. WACC ~9.7%, rounded to 9.5% and held IDENTICAL across bear/base/bull: Melio execution risk, AI disruption and US competitive intensity are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. Lease payments (principal NZ$21.9m, AR line 2837, plus estimated interest ~NZ$8m on NZ$172.3m of liabilities at ~5%; the interest-on-leases line is not separately printed) are charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path at ~0.9% of FY27 revenue, declining to 0.7% as office footprint grows slower than revenue. Lease liabilities are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt, and da_pct_path is D&A ex right-of-use depreciation (FY27 guidance ~NZ$465m includes ~NZ$22m ROU depreciation; ex-ROU ~NZ$443m = 12.1% of FY27 guided revenue). Adjusted EBITDA (36.2% pre-SBC in FY26) is post-IFRS-16, i.e. excludes rent, so the explicit lease charge does not double-count.
inputs.nci_treatment: None. No non-controlling interests; all subsidiaries 100% owned (Melio acquired 100%).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, scenario-weighted (SKILL.md routing row 'Operating company: tech, SaaS'), with the owner-fcf-adaptations applied for (a) NZD flows vs AUD quote and NZD-built WACC, (b) lease treatment (B), (d) interest income stripped with the deposit pile kept in the bridge. Fresh build (first valuation of this ticker; no prior DCF or memory entry). EBITDA margin path is the PRE-SBC adjusted EBITDA margin (FY26 actual 36.2% = adj EBITDA 757.4 + SBC 240.1 over revenue 2,753.1) so the engine's separate SBC deduction reproduces the company's post-SBC adjusted EBITDA. Melio (completed Oct 2025, ~NZ$4.0bn cash + NZ$628m shares + deferred/contingent consideration) contributed NZ$205.0m revenue in ~5.5 months of FY26 (AR line 1597) and is loss-making: group organic adj EBITDA margin was 32.7% vs 27.5% consolidated, implying a Melio FY26 EBITDA drag of ~NZ$75m over the stub period (~NZ$160m annualised). Management guides Melio run-rate adjusted-EBITDA breakeven in H2 FY28. FY27 guidance (AR lines 717-731): revenue NZ$3,620-3,730m, adjusted EBITDA NZ$860-920m including up to ~NZ$55m incremental US brand spend, product capitalisation rate 40-45%, D&A ~NZ$465m. Year-1 drivers are set to that guidance. Cash tax is modelled on EBIT at 32% in FY27-28, falling to 28% by FY32: the group's ANZ/UK profits are taxed at 25-30% while Melio's US losses generate NOLs that do not shelter them until Melio itself is profitable, and the Melio acquired-intangible amortisation inside D&A (~NZ$130m/yr) is unlikely to be fully tax-deductible, which the higher early rate approximates rather than carving D&A for tax separately. Working-capital capture 5% of the revenue increase: subscriptions are billed monthly so deferred revenue is small; FY26 OCF implied ~NZ$48m of working-capital inflow on a NZ$650m revenue increase (~7%). Melio customer funds in transit are excluded from cash and from working capital. Horizon 10 years because the owner-FCF margin is still ramping at year 5 (Melio breakeven, operating leverage, capitalisation rate normalising).

equity_bridge.item: Melio deferred consideration (carrying value, FY26 AR note 20, line 2740)
equity_bridge.note: NZ$83m nominal deferred consideration per the business-combination disclosure; carried at NZ$55.1m. Treated as debt-like cash payable.

equity_bridge.item: Melio contingent consideration (carrying value, FY26 AR note 19, line 2739)
equity_bridge.note: Up to NZ$99m payable on performance conditions; carried at NZ$92.3m (management assesses payment as likely). Treated as debt-like. If settled in shares the dilution would be ~0.9% at the current price, equivalent.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY27 guidance midpoint (+33%) blended with the FY28-FY29 base-case deceleration (22%, 18%) -> ~24% forward 3-year average; cross-checked against the 25-27% historical revenue CAGRs. Equity CAGR is rejected as a growth anchor.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (48.6% 5yr, 72.5% 3yr) is inflated by the A$1.85bn FY26 placement and NZ$628m of Melio consideration shares, not retained earnings; EPS 3yr CAGR is undefined (FY2023 EPS was -0.76 after the FY23 restructuring and Planday/Waddle impairments). Owner-FCF CAGRs are off a tiny base (FY2021 20.4m, FY2023 11.2m) and are not meaningful. Revenue CAGR is the only clean historical series.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income, NZ$m): FY21 20.4, FY22 -53.2, FY23 11.2, FY24 194.9, FY25 237.3, FY26 170.8 (CSV basis; 206.9 on the company FCF definition). Owner FCF FELL in FY26 while reported FCF rose 9%: SBC rose 58% (240.1 vs 151.9, ~45m of it one-off grants) and Melio's stub-period losses were consolidated. SBC has grown faster than FCF over the whole 5-year window (42.7 -> 240.1, 41% CAGR vs reported FCF 50% CAGR off a near-zero base), so an increasing share of the headline FCF growth is being paid for in stock; SBC/revenue has risen from 5.0% (FY21) to 8.7% (FY26), the opposite of the maturing-company pattern.

base.growth_rationale: FY27 +33% sits just below the guidance midpoint (NZ$3,662m vs 3,620-3,730m) and includes a full year of Melio (~NZ$550-600m) plus ~21% organic. FY28 +22% clears the FY28 aspiration (>2x FY25 = >NZ$4,206m) comfortably, as management's aspiration already does on consolidation alone. Deceleration thereafter to 4% by FY36 tracks ANZ saturation (>2m AU customers, 9% customer growth) offset by UK MTD and US payments.
base.margin_rationale: FY27 32.0% pre-SBC = guided adj EBITDA midpoint 24.2% post-SBC + ~7.5% SBC + rounding; the 4pp drop from FY26's 36.2% is the full-year Melio loss and the US brand spend. Ramp to 45% pre-SBC (39.5% post-SBC) by FY36 as Melio reaches breakeven in H2 FY28 and the opex ratio resumes its ~1pp/yr decline; that is below Intuit's ~40%+ non-GAAP operating margin and below Xero's own FY25 organic trajectory extrapolated, so it does not require the US bet to be a large success.
base.capex_da_rationale: FY27 capex 13.5% = product capitalisation back inside the 40-45% range (FY26 was 46.3%, 15.1% capex/revenue) on a growing product spend; D&A 12.1% ex-ROU per the ~NZ$465m guide. Both converge to 10.5% at maturity so the terminal year carries no D&A tax shield beyond replacement capex.

scenario_narratives.base: Xero delivers FY27 guidance (revenue just under the midpoint, adjusted EBITDA at the midpoint after the NZ$55m US brand spend), Melio reaches run-rate EBITDA breakeven in H2 FY28 as guided, and the group resumes ~1pp/yr operating leverage from FY28. ANZ growth slows toward high single digits as the market saturates, the UK keeps growing mid-teens on Making Tax Digital for Income Tax (2026-2028 phases), and the US grows 25-30% organically off a small base without taking meaningful share from QuickBooks. Payments becomes a 15-20% revenue stream by FY30. JAX/AI features defend the bookkeeping workflow rather than expanding ARPC dramatically. SBC normalises from 8.7% (7.1% ex one-offs) to 5.5% of revenue over the decade; the product capitalisation rate returns to 40-45%. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin reaches 45% by FY36 (39.5% post-SBC), still below Intuit today.
scenario_narratives.bull: Melio turns the US into a genuine second core market: accounting-plus-payments bundling lifts US conversion and retention, US revenue compounds at 35-40% for five years, and the ~US$70m of revenue synergies excluded from the FY28 aspiration arrive. UK MTD drives a step-up in sole-trader subscriptions on Xero Simple. AI (JAX) is monetised as premium tiers and an advisory layer, expanding ARPC 8-10%/yr rather than commoditising reconciliation. Group growth stays above 20% through FY29, the opex ratio falls faster than 1pp/yr as US brand spend normalises, and the pre-SBC margin reaches 48% by FY36 with SBC at 5%. The 2026 de-rating reverses as the market re-rates a Rule-of-40 compounder with a dominant ANZ franchise.
scenario_narratives.bear: Melio under-delivers: integration is slower, US payments economics are competed away by Bill.com/Intuit, breakeven slips beyond FY28 and the contingent consideration is paid anyway. Generative-AI tools absorb bookkeeping/reconciliation for micro-businesses, compressing ARPC growth and raising churn in the long tail; AI-native entrants and Intuit's own agents cap Xero's US penetration near 1-2%. ANZ growth decays to mid single digits by FY29 and group growth is below 10% from FY31. The pre-SBC margin plateaus at 37% (30.5% post-SBC, roughly today's organic level), SBC stays above 6.5% of revenue because retention awards are needed in a falling share price, capitalised development stays elevated at 11.5-13.5% of revenue, and the terminal multiple is capped at 16x owner FCF for a structurally slower SaaS asset. Rising AU/NZ bond yields keep the discount rate from falling. This path does not threaten solvency: owner FCF stays positive and the 2031 notes (year-5 put June 2029) can be refinanced or repaid from NZ$1.9bn of liquidity plus cumulative FCF.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 15/50/35 moved to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25% because the thesis now rests on an unproven pivot (a ~NZ$4.6bn US acquisition that is loss-making until H2 FY28, funded by moving from NZ$1.1bn net cash to net debt) and because AI disruption of bookkeeping workflows is a live, non-diversifiable risk to the core product rather than a tail. Bull cut to 25% because it requires several independent things to go right at once: Melio execution, US share gain against Intuit, AI monetisation, and a sector re-rating. No going-concern or covenant risk, so bear is not raised further.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Xero is valued as an operating SaaS company on fully SBC-expensed owner free cash flow, built from components (pre-SBC adjusted EBITDA margin, SBC %, lease charge, D&A, cash tax, capitalised development, working capital on the revenue change) over a 10-year horizon because margins are still ramping through the Melio integration. The house basis treats the NZ$240m of share-based pay as the real cost it is; the street basis (SBC as non-cash) is reported alongside so the reader can see how much of the sell-side's A$85-130 targets depends on that convention. Debt is carried at face (the 2031 convertibles are far out of the money and have a 2029 put), Melio deferred and contingent consideration is deducted, and the WACC is built in NZD and held constant across scenarios so that Melio, AI and US-competition risk are charged once, in the flows and weights. Values are computed in NZD and reported in AUD at the dated NZDAUD rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: Melio integration and breakeven timing: each year of slippage beyond H2 FY28 costs roughly NZ$100-150m of EBITDA and pushes the margin ramp out
AI disruption of core bookkeeping/reconciliation (ARPC compression, long-tail churn) versus AI monetisation through JAX: the single largest swing between bear and bull
US competitive intensity against Intuit QuickBooks; US penetration ~1% and brand spend of NZ$55m in FY27 with uncertain payback
Terminal-value dependence: ~70%+ of EV sits in the terminal value in every scenario; +/-1pp on WACC or terminal growth moves the base IV by ~15-20%
SBC trajectory: SBC/revenue has risen from 5% to 8.7% over five years; if it does not normalise toward 5.5%, house IV falls ~NZ$1/share per 0.5pp
NZD/AUD: a 5% move in the rate moves the AUD IV 5% with no change in the business; the model's constant-currency aspiration uses NZD/AUD 0.91 vs 0.81 today
Pre-results timing: H1 FY27 results (mid-November 2026) will restate the FY27 anchors; the balance sheet used here is 31 March 2026
Platform reliability (May 2026 outages) and US money-transmitter/AML compliance at Melio Solutions Inc.
